commands.grep: Grep, Glob and Read tools only, no shell commands
commands.graphify: graphify explain "<symbol>"            definition line, then every caller (<--) and callee (-->)
commands.semble: semble search "<description>" . -k 5 --max-snippet-lines 0 --format text      search by meaning, prints path:first-last
commands.rust_symbol: codanna retrieve symbol <name>         definition, signature and callers
commands.rust_callers: codanna retrieve callers <name>        every function that calls it
commands.rust_semantic: codanna mcp semantic_search_docs "query:<description>" limit:5      search by meaning
commands.lx1_def: lx def <name>                where a function or class is defined, printed as: name path:first-last
commands.lx1_callers: lx callers <name>            every function that calls it, one per line: name path:first-last
commands.lx1_find: lx find "<description>"      search by meaning, prints path:first-last
commands.lx1_rust: lx find --rust "<description>"      search by meaning, prints: name path:first-last
commands.lx2_def: lx def <name>                where a function or class is defined, printed as: name path:first-last signature
commands.lx2_find: lx find "<description>"      search by meaning, prints: path:first-last, then the functions those lines belong to
commands.lx3_def: lx def <name>...             where each is defined, printed as: name path:first-last signature
commands.lx3_callers: lx callers <name>...         prints "N callers of <name>:" and then one caller per line: name path:first-last
commands.lx3_find: lx find "<description>"      search by meaning, prints: path:first-last of the matching lines, then name:line for each function those lines sit in, where line is the line that function starts on
commands.lx_rust: lx find --rust "<description>"      search by meaning in the Rust index, prints: name path:first-last
commands.lx_about: lx about <name>...           one answer per name: its definition as name path:first-last signature, its doc line, then "N callers:" and one caller per line
commands.lx_cards: lx find --cards "<description>"      search by meaning, prints each hit as the definition it sits in: name path:first-last signature, then that definition's doc line
commands.lx_rust_cards: lx find --rust --cards "<description>"      search by meaning in the Rust index, prints: name path:first-last signature, then the doc line
commands.lx_hybrid: lx find --hybrid "<description>"      search by meaning with two engines merged, prints: name path:first-last signature, then the doc line
commands.lx_hybrid_plain: lx find --hybrid "<description>"      search by meaning, prints: name path:first-last signature, then the doc line
commands.lx_ask: lx ask <kind>:<what>...      several questions in one call, each answer under its own "== kind:what" header. Kinds: def, callers, about (definition, signature, doc line and callers together) and find (search by meaning; quote the whole argument). Example: lx ask about:parse_config callers:load "find:where tokens expire"
commands.tg_symbol: token-goat symbol <name>               where a symbol is defined
commands.tg_callers: token-goat callers <name>              every function that calls it
commands.tg_read: token-goat read "<file>::<symbol>"     the body of one symbol
commands.pgr_about: pgr about <name>...          one answer per name: its definition as name path:first-last signature, then "doc: <line>" when it has a doc line, then "N callers:" and one caller per line as name path:first-last @line (the line the call is on), then "calls:" and the names it calls. A name that is not defined prints "<name>: not found"
commands.pgr_affected: pgr affected <name> [--depth N]   everything that reaches <name> through calls, nearest first. Prints "N affected by <name> (depth D):" and one line per hit: dK name path:first-last via calls @line, where K is the number of calls between them. The default depth is 2
commands.pgr_find: pgr find "<description>"     search by meaning and by words together, prints each hit as the definition it sits in: name path:first-last signature, then its doc line when it has one
commands.pgr_recall: pgr recall "<question>"      notes kept from earlier work in this repository, most relevant first, one per line as: - text  (age ago) #id. A note ends its brackets with "stale: code changed" when code it names has changed since, and "gone: code removed" when that code no longer exists. Prints "no notes" when none match
commands.pgr_ask: pgr ask <kind>:<what>...     several questions in one call, each answer under its own "== kind:what" header. Kinds: about (definition, signature, doc line, callers and what it calls together), callers, def, affected, and find (search by meaning; quote the whole argument). Example: pgr ask about:parse_config callers:load "find:where tokens expire"
commands.pgr_ask_memory: pgr ask <kind>:<what>...     several questions in one call, each answer under its own "== kind:what" header. Kinds: about (definition, signature, doc line, callers and what it calls together), callers, def, affected, and find (search by meaning; quote the whole argument). Example: pgr ask about:parse_config callers:load "find:where tokens expire" When notes kept from earlier work bear on the questions, up to four follow under a closing "== memory" line, one per line as: - text  (age ago) #id. A note ends its brackets with "stale: code changed" when code it names has changed since, and "gone: code removed" when that code no longer exists.
